P1.evidence: The best-run open in the batch. P1b is the only genuine four-part frame anywhere in these twelve files: 'I want to understand, like, what's going on with you, like, what have you tried, where are you trying to get to, and how we can actually help you achieve that' — where you are, what's in the way, where you want to go, what you need. He also set the no-pressure exit properly: 'if not, no worries. We just shake hands and part as friends.' P1c ran explicitly — 'Sounds good?' — and got agreement. P1d immediately after: 'Brief me in. What's going on?' P1a is not applicable rather than a miss: there is no setter on this call, no suffix in the title, and the rep identifies himself as 'the first point of contact' for an inbound prospect who came from Trevor's videos.

P2.evidence: Near-complete and the strongest baseline in the batch. P2a asked directly: 'mind me asking, like, how much do you weigh? What's your height?' P2b is a hit including the desk question — 'What do you do for your living?' then 'there's a lot of sitting as well. I just sit all day' — and he pulled out the 40-minute-each-way commute. P2c is a full hit and rare: 'do you have any other conditions or any limits in your body?', 'But no any serious chronic conditions?', and then hereditary, 'Anything in a family that was in the past, maybe?', which surfaced that both parents are diabetic. P2d ran thoroughly across the back pain, the hips and the mobility limits. P2g covered every meal and the timing of dinner. P2h and P2i both ran — 'how about your, like, with your sleep and energy levels, how does it look like?' followed by 'How do they appear? If you could describe it', which produced the post-lunch lethargy detail. P2f is the one partial: results from current training emerged through the P90X story rather than being asked for.

P3.evidence: Drove all the way through, which is what makes this the deepest call in the batch. P3d ran twice — 'what made it a priority right now for you?' and again at 01:16:32. P3f is a real question rather than an echo: 'you have a one-and-a-half-year-old daughter. Have you thought about her future, like, if you want to show up for her.' That unlocked everything — skiing, tennis, swimming, being older parents. P3g went to legacy explicitly, including using the daughter's name once he asked for it: 'when Shania grows up, and you want to go skiing with her, you can do it.' P3e ran cleanly: 'What would that moment be worth to you?' P3c is met by the triathlon gap he surfaced and the rep pursued with 'would you like to get back to that?' P3h ran as 'your why is going to be your daughter... that will be your main driver for the whole journey' and got explicit agreement, though it is closer to the rep assigning the why than reflecting it back for confirmation. P3a and P3b are partials — the one-thing-you'd-change question was replaced by a weight question, and mobility, strength and energy came from the prospect rather than being offered as options.

P4.evidence: P4c is the standout and the best-handled moment of the phase anywhere in this batch: 'You've been on and off for a while now with this. So help me understand, like, what's kept you from actually changing? Like, where's the missing piece that you didn't stick to it?' When the prospect said he needed to reflect, the rep gave him room — 'Yeah, we have all the time' — and got a two-minute unprompted answer covering work absorption, the missing morning routine, why COVID worked, and 2023. P4a and P4b covered P90X, the isometrics, the dumbbells and the already-purchased kettlebell. P4e landed twice, the second time unprompted and more usefully than the first: 'even when I was doing stuff, I was probably doing it the wrong way. In other words, I was not focusing on form... the functional part of it, and the holistic aspect was missing.' P4f is partial — the scripted 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own' was never asked, though the substance was reached by another route.

P5.evidence: The only call in this batch where the consequence frame actually ran, and it worked. P5a is near-verbatim: 'if you don't take any action now with this, how would it actually going to look like down the line, like one year, two years from now, when you're not making health your priority?' — 'It's only downhill, right?' P5b followed immediately: 'And how does that sit with you, if it's going to be even worse?' — 'I mean, it's terrifying, honestly. The prospect of not being able to do things with my kid, not enjoy the time with her in the future.' That is the phase doing exactly what it is for, and the rep marked it rather than rushing past: 'I got goosebumps, man.' P5c is partial because the why-not was answered without being asked. P5d is a miss — no line in the sand was ever drawn, which matters, because the hesitation that surfaced 25 minutes later was never taken back to this ground.

P6.evidence: Both questions ran and both got clean answers. P6a: 'If you had the right training, simple nutrition, and accountability from Trevor, and everything is going to be built around your life, do you agree that would you get to your goals of putting health as a priority to show up for your family and for yourself?' P6b: 'If you can figure out the details, are you fully committed to showing up and doing the work to become the best version of Gautam...' — 'Absolutely, absolutely. I mean, I have to fix this now.' He also ran a good pre-emptive isolate at 00:39:56: 'is there anything outside of yourself that would stop you from committing actually right now to this fully?' P6c is the miss and it is the pivotal one. Substantial hesitation surfaced after the yes — programme fit for his back, remote delivery, references, and a six-month term he called 'a long time' — and the check says to return to Phase 5 when that happens. He never did. Phase 5 had landed hard 20 minutes earlier and was sitting there unused. Instead he argued for fifteen minutes and then invented a price.

P11.evidence: The most complete P11 in the batch and still incomplete. P11a is a clean hit — the link went into the chat, the prospect paid on the call, and the rep verified it on his end: 'Yeah, it's done.' — 'Okay, cool.' P11b is a hit: the Trevor onboarding was booked live for Monday the 15th at 10:15 Pacific, the confirmation email was verified as received, and the rep walked him through self-rescheduling. P11c is a hard miss and the client is exposed by it — the agreement email never arrived despite repeated checking of inbox and spam, and the rep escalated to a VA on Slack who advised that 'the most important thing is that I got you on the call with Trevor', with the agreement to be sent manually by Angelo 'probably on Monday'. Money was taken with no signed terms. P11d is partial: the Skool community, the onboarding form and app access were all described accurately but none were sent, because they were bundled into the same email that failed.

objection_plays.detail: No money objection at any point. The prospect removed price from the table himself the moment it was presented — 'It's not, not about the, um, I'm not thinking about the money' — and later offered to pay more: 'if that means that there's a higher dollar commitment to getting that comfort level, I'm even willing to work with that.' Worth stating plainly for the rollup: the rep discounted a prospect who had twice said price was not the issue.

Triggered by 'I think I need to do a little more homework on just understanding about Trevor and going over the details' and 'I'll just go look at the testimonials and I'll make my mind up based on that.' Several moves ran and ran well. The isolate ran twice — 'Is there anything coming up for you that's making you ask that?' and 'is something Is coming up that's making you maybe a little bit uncertain after all we've covered?' The thinking-versus-deciding move ran in substance: 'certainty only comes from action, not from thinking about it. Putting more time between taking action and actually making the change.' The version-of-you move ran: 'the version 2.0 of Gautam that is showing up for his family... to make this step without hesitation.' What was missing is the first move — 'Do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal?' — which had been answered yes twenty minutes earlier and was never brought back as the anchor it is meant to be.

The rep diagnosed this as fear and said so: 'I know you're looking for certainty', which is the OE opener asserted rather than asked. The how-will-you-know move ran well — 'ultimately, how are going to actually find out that it's suitable for you? That you're going to be 100% certain before actually committing?' — and produced the prospect's own concession, 'There is no 100% certainty in life, for sure.' None of the other scripted moves ran: no pleasure-versus-pain, no bridge, no plane, no burned-before. The larger problem is diagnostic rather than executional. The prospect corrected the fear reading three separate times — 'That's definitely not what I'm saying', 'there are no red flags that I'm pointing out', 'I think that may not be the question to ask here, right? I mean, I think I've already stated that the motivation is very clear' — and the rep continued running a fear play against a verification request.

SCRIPT GAP, and the most consequential one in this batch — no play exists for a prospect who asks to speak to existing customers. This request occupied roughly fifteen minutes, was raised calmly and repeatedly, and was never answered. With nothing scripted the rep improvised through five distinct positions: a reputation argument, an unprompted 'I'm not AI. I'm not AI. You're talking to a real human', a customer-privacy policy, a hypothetical dismissal ('do you think that I would connect you with someone that wasn't 100% delighted'), and finally the unicorn taunt. He then bypassed it by inventing a one-month tier. The prospect's framing was entirely reasonable and professional — 'I personally, I'm a manager, right? I interview people and I find them very compelling, but I always check references before I pull the trigger. So it's just a standard procedure that I follow' — and the company has no sanctioned answer to it. This is a business asset gap, not a rep failure.

SCRIPT GAP — the known clinical-fit gap, appearing again. The prospect asked directly whether the programme works for someone starting from pain and bad posture, and stated his own view that corrective work should precede loading: 'I feel like that definitely needs something corrective before I start loading.' There is no scripted path for this, so the rep answered with an unevidenced majority claim and a lay biomechanical diagnosis of his own — 'I think this is coming from core. When you have weak core, and when you're putting a lot of weights to do your legs, your core is not supporting that.' No clinician, no assessment, no referral. This is the same gap the playbook already records from the Tyron Giuliani call and it is now the second occurrence in this batch after Fletcher Koder.
No spousal objection. His wife appears only as a co-motivator for the skiing and family goals.
No timing objection. The time-commitment question at 00:40:18 was a practicality check about session length, was answered directly, and never returned.

notes: Phases 1 through 5 are the best work in this batch and P5 in particular finally ran — 'it's terrifying, honestly' is the single most valuable moment across all twelve files. The failure is what happened next. He banked a genuine yes, then let a rational verification request pull him into a fifteen-minute argument he could not win, misdiagnosed it as fear after being corrected three times, and never once went back to the terrifying two-year picture he had already established. The scripted instruction for exactly this situation is P6c: when hesitation surfaces, return to Phase 5. Instead he cut a $6,000 sale to $1,200 for a prospect who had explicitly said money was not the issue and had offered to pay more. Coach the return-to-P5 reflex, and separately escalate the reference gap — no amount of rep skill fixes a company with no referenceable clients.
